## Conversation Context

**I3 — G8 and G9 are never enforced at runtime.**
SPEC §6 says "the build fails if any of these fail," but `cli.run` enforces only G1–G5 (via `check_gates`) and G6/G10 (via `audit`). G7 is legitimately test-only. G8 (`box_snaps` equal across editions) and G9 (no duplicate weeks) are cheap runtime assertions on *this week's* payload — and G9 in particular guards a **live CFBD data event** that a frozen fixture test can never observe. The gate designed to catch a phantom postseason row only ever runs against a fixture. Which, per I2, contains one.
*Fix:* call both from `cli.run` against the built payloads, alongside the G10 check that is already there.

**I4 — The rebuild path silently mislabels the reporting window.**
`payload.py:148-150` builds `epa_by_week` from all of `ppa_games` with no `week <= rw.week` filter, unlike `tempo_rows` (`:174`) which has one. Compounding it, `/stats/season/advanced` and `/ppa/teams` return season-to-date *at call time*: rebuilding week 6 in January pulls full-season numbers. I measured it on the fixture — `baylor_season_adv` reports 923 offensive plays (weeks 1–14) where through week 6 it is 442 — while `meta.season_range` prints "weeks 1–6."
*Why it matters:* `uv run coachreport run --week 6 --season 2025` is a documented, supported path (SPEC §5, README:24), and it produces a page whose stated window contradicts its own numbers. The live Monday path is unaffected because the API has no future data yet.
*Fix:* filter `epa_by_week` by `week <= rw.week` for parity with `tempo_rows`; and document in README that a faithful past-week rebuild is `--offline` (replaying the frozen snapshot), not `--week`.

**I5 — `templates/performance.tpl.html:674-675` hardcodes the preposition "at".**
`` `Our offensive snaps at ${D.meta.next_opponent}` ``. `meta.next_home` is derived and unused; `meta.next_game` already carries the right word. Wrong roughly half the weeks. Same root cause as C1: orientation keys delivered and ignored.
*Fix:* `${D.meta.next_home ? "vs" : "at"}`, or reuse `next_short`.

**I6 — `test_a_broken_page_makes_the_gates_fail` is satisfiable by the gates not running.** Deferred #19, confirmed live. `tests/test_pdf.py:59-63` — the single `ProbeFailed` fallback string contains "G2", "G3" and "G4". Add `assert "could not be measured" not in joined`.

**I7 — DESIGN.md:76-79 still instructs verification via `document.fonts.check()`** — the API this build proved returns `true` for fonts that do not exist. A maintainer following the design doc would rebuild the vacuous gate. Same paragraph names a script path that no longer exists.

**I8 — `pdf.py` reads and writes HTML without `encoding="utf-8"`** (`:103` twice, `:121`), against CLAUDE.md's own stated invariant, in the module a Phase-2 launchd agent will run under a bare environment. `render.py:24, 27` gets it right — the inconsistency is the tell.

### Minor

- **M1** — `payload.py:183`: `series[r["name"]][week] = snaps` is last-write-wins across a player's position rows, where `pff.season_snap_rows` explicitly groups by `(name, position, week)` and the coaches edition takes a `max` over the same quantity (`:104`). Zero occurrences in the fixture, so it is latent — but a mid-season position change would silently undercount a player's week *and* make the output input-order-dependent, defeating the shuffle-determinism test. Take a `max`, and key by `(name, position)` or a player id if PFF exposes one.
- **M2** — `audit.no_tier_language` scans the entire payload, including raw CFBD `playText`. A play description containing "weak" or "soft" would hard-fail the Monday build over data Baylor doesn't control, with no override. G10's stated scope is *generated player copy*.
- **M3** — `snapshot.py:35`: `p4_distributions` silently narrows the comparison set when `/teams/fbs` is incomplete. The sheet prints `p4_n` as a fact; a floor check belongs in C2's completeness gate.
- **M4** — `resolve.py:34-36` is the second `seasonType` filter that CLAUDE.md calls a spec violation. Harmless; align doc or code.
- **M5** — `render.py:14` and `cli.py:82,88` use `json.dumps(..., default=str)`, which silently stringifies any unexpected type (a DuckDB `Decimal`, a datetime) rather than raising. The fixture shows clean floats today, so nothing is broken — but it is a silent-coercion hazard on a payload whose numbers are printed.
- **M6** — `"Sheet 5 of 5"` is static markup in both templates (`coaches:353`, `performance:311`). Harmless while G1 pins the count at 5; in the accepted 6-page finale case it prints a lie next to a failing gate. One new wrinkle on an already-accepted item, not a re-litigation.
- **M7** — Nothing gates the `--no-pdf-header-footer` behavior. Chrome ignores unknown flags in silence; if that flag is ever renamed, a `file:///…` footer appears on the printed handout with every gate green. A one-line `assert "file://" not in dumped_text` in the probe would close it.
- **M8** — `templates/coaches.tpl.html` uses the literal "Baylor" 22 times where `M.team` is available and used once. Harmless (TEAM is the one legitimate constant) but inconsistent with SPEC §1.1's "lives in `config.py`."
- **M9** — Doc drift: SPEC G7 names `tests/fixtures/snapshot.json` (actual: `snapshot_2025w06.json`); CLAUDE.md says the suite takes ~60s (measured: 34s).</result>

`payload.py:148-150` builds `epa_by_week` from all of `ppa_games` with no `week <= rw.week` filter, unlike `tempo_rows` (`:174`) which has one. Compounding it, `/stats/season/advanced` and `/ppa/teams` return season-to-date *at call time*: rebuilding week 6 in January pulls full-season numbers. I measured it on the fixture — `baylor_season_adv` reports 923 offensive plays (weeks 1–14) where through week 6 it is 442 — while `meta.season_range` prints "weeks 1–6."

## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
